intro.say: {name}. Good, you're awake. Don't sit down, there isn't time. You heard the pumps stop in the night.

opts.t: I heard Pell swearing at them since midnight.

recycler.say: The coolant regulator in the water recycler cracked. Pell says it can't be patched again, and there is no spare. We have nine days of clean water. Four hundred people.

plan.say: Before the war, a plant called Meridian Atomics used the same regulator. If one still exists, it is up there. I am opening the door, {name}. I am sending you.

whyme.say: Because you had the best marks in Security training in forty years. And because you are the only one who ever asked me what the sky looks like. Now you get to find out.

refuse.say: Then four hundred people die of thirst slowly, and you with them. I would rather you went up there with a pistol and my blessing.

orders.say: Draw your gear from the Security locker across the corridor. Pell wants a word before you leave. Then the great door. Once it closes behind you, it stays closed until you come home with that part.

hub.say: Locker, Pell, then the door. Nine days, {name}.

surface.say: Our records say the bombs took everything. They also say the coffee machine was repaired in 2061, so believe what you like. Just come home.

intro.say: Don't touch that, it's holding the other thing together. You're the one going up? Then listen. Coolant regulator, model R-7. Size of a loaf of bread, twice as heavy, Meridian stamp on the housing. Nothing else will fit.

opts.t: Can't you fix the old one?

fix.say: I've fixed it nine times. It isn't a part any more, it's a memory of one. One more crack and the loop floods with silt. Bring me a new one.

tips.say: The surface has weather. I've read about it. Apparently it just happens to you. Keep your water clean and your pistol cleaner. Find a workbench and tune that thing before it tunes you.

gift.say: Here. Tape and scrap. Everything up there is broken, so you'll want to be able to fix things. Good luck.

hub.say: R-7. Meridian stamp. Don't come back with a toaster.

intro.say: There you are, sweet pea. The Overseer told me everything, and I told her she was a fool, and then I packed you a lunch. Two stews and a tin of the meat nobody asks about.

bye.say: You come back to us. And if the sky really is blue up there, you remember it for me.

hurt.say: Pride is heavy, {name}, and you'll be carrying enough up there. Take it anyway.

hub.say: Go on, before I start crying into the soup.
Ah, {name}. You were always the one staring out of the window that wasn't there. Off somewhere important?

opts.t: What are the children learning today?

over.say: Then go. And remember what I taught you: measure twice, trust once, and never drink anything that glows.

lesson.say: Arithmetic, water rationing, and the history of the surface. The official version. I keep the unofficial version in a drawer.

after.say: You came back. The children talk about nothing else. Tell me, is the sky really that big?

hub.say: Haven 12 clinic. If you're bleeding, sit. If you're not, I'm very busy pretending to be.

health.say: Fine, except for the water. Every percent the recycler loses, I see it a week later. Kidneys first. Then tempers.

advice.say: Radiation is patient and you are not. Carry Lead Tabs, don't drink from puddles that hum, and if a dog has two heads, believe the other dog.

ml.say: Every shift wrote its log by hand: pressures, temperatures, who was on duty. If someone kept writing that last night, we would finally know whether Meridian failed, or was failed. The control rooms are near the core.

mldone.say: "Coolant pumps 2 and 3 cut by remote command. Not us. Not us." They knew. Somebody sent that order from outside. Thank you. History is a terrible gift, but it is a gift. Take this, for the road.

hub.say: Careful with the tomatoes. They've had a hard year. Haven't we all.

opts.t: How does anything grow down here?

grow.say: Grow lights, recycled water and a lot of shouting. The lights are pre-war. When the last bulb goes, we eat moss. Find me seeds up there, would you? Real ones.

vs.say: Would you? Real seeds, with the life still in them. Our strains are forty years tired. Ranchers keep seed stock, if there are any ranchers left.

vsdone.say: Beans. Squash. Real maize! Oh, the children are going to eat something green that isn't algae. Haven 12 owes you twice now.

surf.say: Once, on the last water run. Twenty years ago. Saw a bird. It looked at me like I owed it money.

dunn.say: Me? Leave Haven 12? I... I've been guarding a locker for twenty years. Is it a real town? With real problems?

dunnyes.say: A real sky. All right. I'll pack tonight. Tell the Mayor I'm slow, but I'm thorough.

hub.say: Today's special is algae loaf. Yesterday's special was also algae loaf. I believe in consistency.

meat.say: Bring me a steak from the surface and I will cook it so well the Overseer will weep. Then I will eat it in front of her.

rm.say: A steak. An actual steak. Bring me one and I will make the Overseer cry, and then I will make you a stew so good you will forget the surface exists.

rmdone.say: Look at the marbling. LOOK at it. I am going to cry first, actually. Here, stew. Three bowls. Come back for the steak dinner; I am inviting the whole vault.
